John 1:1.nt_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
John 1:1.oldest_manuscript: Papyrus 66 (P66) — approximately 200 CE — 170 years after events described
John 1:1.authorship: Anonymous. The name John was assigned by Irenaeus of Lyon approximately 180 CE for theological reasons stated explicitly in his writing Adversus Haereses. The manuscript itself carries no author name.
John 1:1.greco_roman_parallel: Logos theology — Greek philosophical concept developed by Heraclitus (500 BCE) and Philo of Alexandria (20 BCE-50 CE). Philo explicitly used the term Logos as a divine intermediary figure in Greek philosophical Judaism. The opening of John replicates Philo's Logos framework, not any DSS or Orit Ge'ez concept.
John 1:1.dss_contradiction: Bereshit 1:1 — DSS Genesis scrolls Cave 4: In the beginning The Creator created the heavens and the earth. YHWH acts directly. There is no pre-existent divine Word figure anywhere in the primary source corpus. Yeshayahu 43:10-11 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: Before Me no god was formed nor shall there be any after Me. I YHWH am the only one and besides Me there is no saviour. This is an absolute statement. No divine Word co-equal with YHWH exists in any DSS or Orit Ge'ez text.
John 1:1.verdict: Constructed from Greek Logos philosophy. No DSS or Orit Ge'ez source. Directly contradicted by the primary source absolute monotheism of Yeshayahu 43:10-11 confirmed in 1QIsa-a Cave 1.

Matthew 1:23.nt_text: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel.
Matthew 1:23.authorship: Anonymous. Name Matthew assigned by Irenaeus of Lyon 180 CE. No manuscript carries this name in original form.
Matthew 1:23.original_dss_reading: Yeshayahu 7:14 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1 — the Great Isaiah Scroll, oldest complete biblical manuscript in existence, dated 125-100 BCE: Behold the almah shall conceive and bear a son and shall call his name Immanuel.
Matthew 1:23.manipulation: FABRICATED FROM MISTRANSLATION. The Hebrew word in 1QIsa-a is almah — young woman of marriageable age. The ancient Hebrew word for virgin is betulah — a completely different word that does not appear in this verse in any ancient manuscript. The Greek Septuagint translated almah as parthenos — virgin — a translation decision made approximately 200 BCE. Matthew's author used the Greek Septuagint reading, not the Hebrew original. The DSS primary witness — written before the Septuagint translation became standard — confirms almah not betulah.
Matthew 1:23.historical_context: Yeshayahu 7:14 in its original context is addressed to King Ahaz of Yehudah during the Syro-Ephraimite crisis approximately 735 BCE. The young woman was contemporary to Ahaz. The child's birth was a sign to Ahaz about events happening in his lifetime. It is not a prediction about a birth 700 years later. The DSS context confirms this historical reading.
Matthew 1:23.verdict: Built on a Greek mistranslation of almah to parthenos. The DSS primary source 1QIsa-a says young woman. No virgin birth exists in any primary source manuscript.

John 3:16.nt_text: For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish but have everlasting life.
John 3:16.greco_roman_parallel: The dying and rising divine son sent by a divine father is documented in Osiris-Horus tradition (Egyptian), Dionysus tradition (Greek), and Mithras tradition (Persian-Roman). All predate this text by centuries. The concept of salvation through the blood of a divine son was present in multiple Greco-Roman mystery religion traditions operating simultaneously in the Mediterranean world where this text was written.
John 3:16.dss_contradiction: Yeshayahu 43:11 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: I YHWH am the only one and besides Me there is no saviour. Daniyyel 2:22 — DSS Daniyyel Cave 4: He reveals deep and hidden things. YHWH is the direct actor. Chanokh 41:9 — Orit Ge'ez: YHWH does not need an intermediary. He knows all things before they happen. No intermediary divine son figure exists anywhere in the primary source corpus.
John 3:16.verdict: No primary source. Constructed in Greco-Roman world with direct parallels to pre-existing Mediterranean dying-rising son theology. Directly contradicted by the absolute monotheism of the DSS and Orit Ge'ez primary sources.

1 John 5:7.nt_text: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one.
1 John 5:7.oldest_manuscript: This verse does not appear in any Greek manuscript before the 4th century CE. It does not appear in any early church father writing before the 4th century CE. It first appears in a Latin manuscript — Codex Fuldensis — approximately 546 CE. It was inserted into the Greek text by scribes under institutional pressure.
1 John 5:7.authorship: Anonymous. Name John assigned 180 CE. This specific verse was added by unknown scribes centuries after the base text was written.
1 John 5:7.manipulation: INSERTION. Erasmus of Rotterdam compiled the Greek NT in 1516 and omitted this verse because it appeared in no Greek manuscript he could find. Church authorities pressured him to include it. He stated he would include it if a single Greek manuscript could be found containing it. A manuscript was produced — now identified as Codex Montfortianus, written specifically to pressure Erasmus. He included it under protest. Modern textual scholars universally identify this verse as a late insertion. It is absent from all modern critical Greek NT editions.
1 John 5:7.dss_contradiction: Yeshayahu 43:10-11 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: Before Me no god was formed nor shall there be any after Me. I YHWH am the only one. Devarim 6:4 — DSS Nash Papyrus and 4Q fragments: Hear O Yisra'el YHWH is our Creator YHWH is One. The Trinity formulation of three co-equal divine persons was formalized at Nicaea 325 CE by political vote under Emperor Constantine. It contradicts the absolute monotheism of the primary sources at every point.
1 John 5:7.verdict: Documented insertion. Not in earliest manuscripts. Not in earliest church writings. Added by scribes under institutional pressure. Directly contradicted by the absolute monotheism confirmed in 1QIsa-a Cave 1 and the DSS Nash Papyrus.

Matthew 27:46.nt_text: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
Matthew 27:46.original_dss_reading: Tehillim 22:1 — 11QPs Great Psalms Scroll Cave 11: My El, my El, why have you forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my cry.
Matthew 27:46.manipulation: PHRASE EXTRACTION with suppression of context. Tehillim 22 is a communal lament psalm that ends in vindication and praise. Verse 24 states explicitly: He has not despised nor scorned the suffering of the afflicted one. He has not hidden His face from him but has listened to his cry for help. The psalm resolves in YHWH answering. The NT narrative extracts only the opening cry of abandonment and presents it as the final word. The resolution — YHWH hears and answers — was suppressed because it contradicted the theological narrative being constructed. The full psalm in 11QPs contradicts the abandonment theology built from the extracted phrase.
Matthew 27:46.verdict: Taken from Tehillim 22:1 in 11QPs Cave 11. The surrounding context suppressed. The psalm itself contradicts the abandonment narrative in verse 24.

Isaiah 53.nt_text: Applied throughout NT as prophecy of individual suffering saviour figure.
Isaiah 53.oldest_manuscript: 1QIsa-a Cave 1 — the Great Isaiah Scroll — 125-100 BCE — primary DSS witness
Isaiah 53.original_dss_reading: The servant in Yeshayahu 40-55 is identified as Yisra'el explicitly and repeatedly in the surrounding text. Yeshayahu 41:8: But you Yisra'el are My servant. Yeshayahu 44:1: But now hear O Yaakov My servant and Yisra'el whom I have chosen. Yeshayahu 49:3: And He said to me You are My servant O Yisra'el in whom I will be glorified. The servant is a collective national figure throughout the entire literary unit. Chapter 53 is part of this continuous literary unit.
Isaiah 53.manipulation: FULL PASSAGE REFRAME. The collective national servant of the surrounding 15 chapters was individualized into a single person. The literary context was severed. The surrounding chapters which identify the servant as Yisra'el explicitly were ignored. The NT application of this passage to an individual required removing it from its literary context entirely.
Isaiah 53.dss_contradiction: 1QIsa-a contains no individual messianic figure in chapter 53. The DSS pesher tradition does not interpret Isaiah 53 as predicting an individual saviour. The Qumran community who wrote and preserved the DSS did not make this connection. The individual suffering saviour interpretation was constructed by later communities operating outside the primary source tradition.
Isaiah 53.verdict: Taken from 1QIsa-a Cave 1 and reframed from collective national servant to individual. The surrounding literary context which identifies the servant as Yisra'el collectively was suppressed.

Hebrews 1:3.nt_text: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power.
Hebrews 1:3.authorship: Anonymous. Hebrews explicitly does not claim Pauline authorship in its text. The church assigned it to Paul despite significant differences in vocabulary, style, and theology from the undisputed Pauline letters. Origen of Alexandria (185-254 CE) wrote: who actually wrote the epistle only YHWH knows. The book is anonymous.
Hebrews 1:3.greco_roman_parallel: The image of a divine being as the exact imprint or radiance of a divine father is Platonic philosophy. Philo of Alexandria used identical language — apaugasma (radiance) and charakter (exact imprint) — to describe the Logos figure in his philosophical writings. These are Greek philosophical terms, not Hebrew covenantal terms. The author of Hebrews was demonstrably operating in the Philonic philosophical tradition, not the DSS tradition.
Hebrews 1:3.dss_contradiction: No divine radiance figure exists in any DSS or Orit Ge'ez text. YHWH has no divine son who upholds all things in the primary source corpus. Yeshayahu 43:10-11 — 1QIsa-a: I YHWH am the only saviour. Devarim 6:4 — DSS Nash Papyrus: YHWH is One.
Hebrews 1:3.verdict: No primary source. Constructed from Platonic and Philonic Greek philosophy. Directly contradicted by primary source monotheism.

Revelation 22:16.nt_text: I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.
Revelation 22:16.authorship: Anonymous. The name John was assigned. The text itself claims to be written by one called John in exile on Patmos. No external evidence confirms this is the same John as any gospel.
Revelation 22:16.primary_source_connection: Bamidbar 24:17 — claimed — a star shall come out of Yaakov and a scepter shall rise out of Yisra'el
Revelation 22:16.original_dss_reading: Bamidbar 24:17 — DSS Numbers scrolls: A star shall come out of Yaakov and a scepter shall rise out of Yisra'el. In the DSS corpus this verse is interpreted in the War Scroll 1QM and the Damascus Document as referring to a human royal leader of the covenant community — not a divine figure. The morning star designation in the primary source tradition refers to Babylon in Yeshayahu 14:12 — how you have fallen from heaven O morning star son of the dawn — a taunt against the king of Babylon.
Revelation 22:16.manipulation: FABRICATED FROM REFRAMING. The morning star in Yeshayahu 14:12 in the DSS tradition refers to Babylon's king brought low. The scepter of Bamidbar 24:17 in the DSS War Scroll is a human military leader. The NT appropriates both and merges them into a divine figure claim.
Revelation 22:16.verdict: Built from misapplication of two primary source passages. Both passages in their DSS context refer to human figures. The divine morning star claim is not in any primary source.

Matthew 28:19.nt_text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
Matthew 28:19.manipulation: The Trinitarian baptismal formula — Father, Son, and Holy Ghost — does not appear in the earlier Acts of the Apostles which describes baptism in the name of Yeshua only. The two formulas contradict each other within the NT itself. Church historian Eusebius of Caesarea — writing before 325 CE — quotes this verse more than 20 times in his writings and consistently quotes it without the Trinitarian formula. His pre-Nicaea version reads: Go and make disciples of all nations in my name. The Trinitarian formula appears to have been inserted after Nicaea 325 CE when the Trinity was formalized as doctrine.
Matthew 28:19.dss_contradiction: Devarim 6:4 — DSS Nash Papyrus: YHWH is One. No Trinitarian formula exists anywhere in the DSS or Orit Ge'ez corpus. The divine name used in covenant initiation throughout the primary sources is YHWH alone.
Matthew 28:19.verdict: No primary source. Trinitarian formula contradicted by earlier NT texts. Likely inserted post-Nicaea 325 CE. Directly contradicted by primary source monotheism of Devarim 6:4.

Luke 1:35.nt_text: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
Luke 1:35.authorship: Anonymous. Name Luke assigned by church tradition. The text itself is anonymous.
Luke 1:35.primary_source_connection: NONE — the divine conception claim has no DSS or Orit Ge'ez source
Luke 1:35.greco_roman_parallel: Divine conception — a god impregnating a human woman to produce a divine-human offspring — is one of the most common motifs in Greco-Roman religion. Zeus and Semele produced Dionysus. Zeus and Alcmene produced Heracles. Osiris and Isis produced Horus. The Romans deified Julius Caesar and Augustus as sons of gods. The concept was culturally dominant in the Mediterranean world where Luke was written.
Luke 1:35.dss_contradiction: The DSS contain no divine conception narrative anywhere. The Orit Ge'ez contains no divine conception narrative anywhere. Devarim 18:20-22 — DSS Torah: the prophet who speaks what YHWH has not commanded shall die. Yeshayahu 7:14 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: the almah — young woman — conceives by natural means. The primary sources describe no supernatural human conception at any point.
Luke 1:35.verdict: No primary source. Directly parallels pre-existing Greco-Roman divine conception traditions that predate this text by centuries. No DSS or Orit Ge'ez basis.

Romans 5:12.nt_text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.
Romans 5:12.authorship: The letter claims Pauline authorship and is among the undisputed Pauline letters stylistically. However the theological conclusion drawn from verse 12 by Augustine of Hippo in 397 CE is not in the Greek original.
Romans 5:12.primary_source_connection: NONE for the original sin doctrine built from this verse
Romans 5:12.manipulation: FABRICATED FROM MISTRANSLATION. The Greek text reads: eph ho pantes hemarton meaning because all sinned or in that all sinned. Jerome's Latin Vulgate translated this as in quo omnes peccaverunt meaning in whom all sinned — projecting inherited guilt from Adam onto all humanity. Augustine built the entire doctrine of original sin from Jerome's Latin mistranslation. The Greek original says death spread because all sin individually. The Vulgate says death spread because all sinned in Adam. Completely different meaning from a single translation decision.
Romans 5:12.dss_contradiction: Community Rule 1QS Column 3 — Cave 1: YHWH appointed two spirits within human beings. Each person walks in the spirit they have been given. The DSS framework is individual moral responsibility not inherited guilt. 4QInstruction 4Q417 — Cave 4: You are responsible for the spirit placed within you. Guard it. This is individual accountability not collective inherited sin.
Romans 5:12.greco_roman_parallel: None directly. The doctrine of original sin is Augustine's 4th century CE construction from a Latin translation error. It has no parallel in Greek philosophy or Greco-Roman religion and no basis in the DSS or Orit Ge'ez.
Romans 5:12.verdict: The doctrine of original sin built from this verse rests entirely on Jerome's mistranslation of the Greek eph ho as in whom rather than because. The DSS Community Rule and 4QInstruction confirm individual moral responsibility not inherited guilt. Augustine's doctrine has no primary source basis.

John 14:6.nt_text: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
John 14:6.authorship: Anonymous. Name John assigned by Irenaeus 180 CE. No manuscript carries this name in original form.
John 14:6.greco_roman_parallel: The concept of a divine intermediary as the exclusive path to the divine father is present in multiple Greco-Roman mystery religion traditions. Mithraism presented Mithras as the mediator between humanity and Ahura Mazda. The Hermetic tradition presented Hermes as the guide to divine knowledge. None of these predate the NT claim with identical language but the mediator-as-exclusive-path concept was culturally dominant.
John 14:6.dss_contradiction: Yeshayahu 55:6 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: Seek YHWH while He may be found. Call upon Him while He is near. YHWH is directly accessible. No intermediary required. Tehillim 145:18 — 11QPs Cave 11: YHWH is near to all who call on Him, to all who call on Him in truth. Near to all. No qualifying intermediary stated. Devarim 4:29 — DSS Deuteronomy: You will seek YHWH your Creator and you will find Him if you search after Him with all your heart and soul. Direct access. No intermediary.
John 14:6.verdict: No primary source. Concept of exclusive divine intermediary contradicts the direct access to YHWH stated throughout the DSS corpus. YHWH is near to all who call on Him in truth — no qualifying intermediary appears anywhere in the primary sources.

Colossians 1:15-16.nt_text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature: For by him were all things created.
Colossians 1:15-16.authorship: Deutero-Pauline. Colossians is one of six letters attributed to Paul that stylometric analysis identifies as written by a different author after Paul's death. The vocabulary, sentence structure, and Christology are inconsistent with the undisputed Pauline letters. Most NT scholars do not attribute Colossians to Paul.
Colossians 1:15-16.greco_roman_parallel: Image of the invisible God — this is Platonic philosophical language. Philo of Alexandria used eikon tou theou — image of God — to describe the Logos figure in identical terms. This is Greek metaphysics applied to a Jewish figure, not anything from the DSS or Orit Ge'ez tradition. Firstborn of all creation as a divine creative agent parallels the Logos of Philo and the Sophia figure of Hellenistic Jewish wisdom literature.
Colossians 1:15-16.dss_contradiction: Bereshit 1:1 — DSS Genesis: In the beginning The Creator created. YHWH creates directly. No pre-existent divine agent creates on His behalf in any DSS or Orit Ge'ez text. Yeshayahu 44:24 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: I am YHWH who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by Myself. By Myself. No creative intermediary.
Colossians 1:15-16.verdict: Deutero-Pauline — not written by Paul. Built from Platonic and Philonic Greek philosophy. Directly contradicted by Yeshayahu 44:24 in 1QIsa-a which states YHWH created alone by Himself with no divine intermediary.

Philippians 2:6.nt_text: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God.
Philippians 2:6.authorship: This letter is among the undisputed Pauline letters but the Christological hymn in verses 6-11 is widely identified by scholars as a pre-Pauline liturgical fragment Paul incorporated. The hymn predates the letter itself.
Philippians 2:6.greco_roman_parallel: Divine beings who temporarily take human form and then return to divine status is a standard motif in Greco-Roman mythology. Zeus, Dionysus, and multiple other deities appear in human form in the literature of the period. The concept of a divine being emptying himself of divine prerogatives to take human form has no parallel in any DSS or Orit Ge'ez text.
Philippians 2:6.dss_contradiction: Yeshayahu 43:10 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: Before Me no god was formed nor shall there be any after Me. No figure equal with YHWH exists in any form. Devarim 4:35 — DSS Deuteronomy: YHWH He is The Creator. There is no other besides Him. No second divine person equal with YHWH appears anywhere in the primary sources.
Philippians 2:6.verdict: No primary source. The concept of equality with YHWH is explicitly impossible within the absolute monotheism of the DSS. Yeshayahu 43:10 in 1QIsa-a is an absolute statement that allows no equal divine figure.

Hebrews 7:3.nt_text: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
Hebrews 7:3.authorship: Anonymous. Hebrews does not claim Pauline authorship in the text. Origen stated explicitly that only YHWH knows who wrote it. The church assigned it to Paul without manuscript evidence.
Hebrews 7:3.original_dss_reading: Bereshit 14:18-20 — DSS Genesis: Malkitzedeq king of Shalem brought out bread and wine. He was a priest of El Elyon. He blessed Avram. In the DSS 11QMelchizedek scroll from Cave 11 Malkitzedeq is an exalted angelic figure who executes divine judgment in the final days. He is not described as without father without mother without beginning or end. He is an exalted created being not an eternal divine person.
Hebrews 7:3.manipulation: FULL PASSAGE REFRAME. The Hebrews author takes the silence of the Bereshit text about Malkitzedeq's genealogy — the text simply does not mention his parents — and constructs a theological argument that this silence means he had no parents and no beginning or end. This is an argument from silence elevated into a theological claim. The 11QMelchizedek DSS scroll describes Malkitzedeq as a powerful angelic being. Not as an eternal divine person without origin.
Hebrews 7:3.dss_contradiction: 11QMelchizedek — Cave 11 Qumran: Malkitzedeq is an exalted angelic figure appointed for the final judgment. He is a created being exalted to a high position. He is not without beginning. He is not eternal. He is not equal to YHWH. The DSS text that most extensively discusses Malkitzedeq directly contradicts the Hebrews interpretation.
Hebrews 7:3.verdict: Built on an argument from silence in Bereshit. The DSS 11QMelchizedek scroll — the primary source that actually discusses Malkitzedeq extensively — presents him as an exalted created angelic being, not an eternal divine person. The Hebrews claim has no primary source support.

Acts 2:38.nt_text: Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins.
Acts 2:38.authorship: Anonymous. Luke-Acts is a two-part work by the same anonymous author. The name Luke was assigned by tradition.
Acts 2:38.primary_source_connection: NONE — the concept of remission of sins through baptism in a personal name has no DSS or Orit Ge'ez basis
Acts 2:38.dss_contradiction: Tehillim 103:3 — 11QPs Cave 11: He forgives all your transgressions. YHWH forgives directly. No ritual water immersion in a personal name is required in any primary source text. The DSS community practiced ritual immersion — mikveh — for purity purposes but this was repeated purification not a one-time remission of sins through a personal name. Words of the Luminaries 4QDibHam — Cave 4: Direct prayer of confession to YHWH for forgiveness. No intermediary ritual required.
Acts 2:38.verdict: No primary source. YHWH forgives directly in every DSS and Orit Ge'ez text. No one-time ritual immersion in a personal name appears anywhere in the primary corpus.

Revelation 1:8.nt_text: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, saith the Lord, which is, and which was, and which is to come, the Almighty.
Revelation 1:8.authorship: Anonymous. The text claims to be written by a John in exile on Patmos. No external evidence confirms identity.
Revelation 1:8.primary_source_connection: Yeshayahu 44:6 — claimed — I am the first and I am the last
Revelation 1:8.original_dss_reading: Yeshayahu 44:6 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: I am the first and I am the last and besides Me there is no god. This statement is made by YHWH about YHWH alone. It is an absolute monotheism statement. The surrounding context in Yeshayahu 44 is an extended argument against idolatry.
Revelation 1:8.manipulation: APPROPRIATED and reapplied. The first and last declaration of YHWH from 1QIsa-a is applied to the figure described in Revelation. The Greek Alpha and Omega replaces the Hebrew first and last. The original statement is a declaration of YHWH's absolute uniqueness with no equal. The Revelation application transfers this uniqueness declaration to a second figure — which directly contradicts the meaning of the original statement which denies the existence of any other such figure.
Revelation 1:8.verdict: The YHWH uniqueness declaration from 1QIsa-a is applied to a second figure. This use directly contradicts the original statement which declares YHWH alone is first and last with no other beside Him.

Matthew 5:17.nt_text: Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
Matthew 5:17.dss_contradiction: The concept of a single person fulfilling the Torah and thereby completing or superseding it is not in any DSS or Orit Ge'ez text. Community Rule 1QS Column 1 — Cave 1: to walk perfectly in all His ways as He commanded through Moshe and through all His servants the prophets. The covenant community studies and walks in Torah. No single person fulfils it on behalf of others. Yovelim 2:33 — Orit Ge'ez: The Sabbath is for all generations forever. Not until a person fulfils it. Forever.
Matthew 5:17.verdict: No primary source for the fulfil and thereby complete concept. The DSS community studied Torah as an ongoing communal practice with no concept of a single person's fulfilment replacing that practice.

Mark 16:16.nt_text: He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
Mark 16:16.oldest_manuscript: This verse is part of the Long Ending of Mark (16:9-20) which does not appear in Codex Sinaiticus or Codex Vaticanus — the two oldest and most complete manuscripts. It was added by scribes. Modern translations footnote this.
Mark 16:16.authorship: Anonymous. Name Mark assigned by tradition. This specific passage is a scribal addition not in the original text.
Mark 16:16.manipulation: INSERTION. The two oldest complete manuscripts of Mark end at 16:8 with an empty tomb and frightened women. The Long Ending containing this verse was added by later scribes. This is not disputed. It is noted in footnotes of modern translations including the NIV, ESV, and NRSV. The verse presents a salvation formula that does not appear in the original Mark text.
Mark 16:16.dss_contradiction: No salvation formula requiring belief in a specific person plus ritual water immersion appears anywhere in the DSS or Orit Ge'ez corpus. Tehillim 34:8 — 11QPs: Taste and see that YHWH is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him. Refuge in YHWH directly. No qualifying belief statement or ritual.
Mark 16:16.verdict: A scribal insertion not present in the oldest manuscripts. Not part of the original Mark text. No primary source basis for the salvation formula it presents.

Luke 2:11.nt_text: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
Luke 2:11.authorship: Anonymous. Name Luke assigned by tradition.
Luke 2:11.primary_source_connection: NONE — a divine saviour born in human history has no DSS or Orit Ge'ez source
Luke 2:11.greco_roman_parallel: The birth announcement of a divine saviour figure was a standard Roman imperial formula. Augustus Caesar was called Soter — Saviour — and his birth was announced as bringing peace and salvation to the world. The Roman imperial cult used identical language for the emperor. The announcement formula in Luke 2 mirrors Roman imperial birth announcements that were publicly displayed across the empire at the time of writing.
Luke 2:11.dss_contradiction: Yeshayahu 43:11 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: I YHWH am the only Saviour. Absolute. No human saviour born in any city. Tehillim 27:1 — 11QPs Cave 11: YHWH is my light and my salvation. YHWH is salvation directly. No birth announcement of a human saviour figure appears anywhere in the primary source corpus.
Luke 2:11.verdict: No primary source. Roman imperial birth announcement formula applied to a religious figure. Directly contradicted by Yeshayahu 43:11 in 1QIsa-a which states YHWH alone is Saviour.

John 20:28.nt_text: And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
John 20:28.dss_contradiction: Devarim 6:4 — DSS Nash Papyrus: YHWH is our Creator YHWH is One. Calling a human figure My God is a direct violation of the absolute monotheism of the primary sources. Yeshayahu 42:8 — 1QIsa-a Cave 1: I am YHWH that is My name. I will not give My glory to another. My name cannot be applied to another being. The divine address My God applied to a human figure is impossible within the primary source theological framework.
John 20:28.verdict: No primary source. The divine address applied to a human figure directly contradicts the absolute monotheism of Devarim 6:4 and Yeshayahu 42:8 confirmed in the DSS Nash Papyrus and 1QIsa-a Cave 1.

Galatians 3:13.nt_text: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.
Galatians 3:13.original_dss_reading: Devarim 21:22-23 — DSS Deuteronomy: If a man has committed a sin worthy of death and he is put to death and you hang him on a tree his corpse shall not hang overnight on the tree but you shall surely bury him on the same day for he who is hanged is accursed of The Creator. This passage governs the post-execution hanging of a criminal's body as a public deterrent. It is not a redemption theology.
Galatians 3:13.manipulation: FULL PASSAGE REFRAME. A practical legal provision about the post-execution display of a criminal's body is reframed as a mechanism for cosmic redemption. The original context is about the dignity of burial and the defilement of the land by leaving a body exposed. Paul applies it to construct a substitutionary atonement theology that has no basis in the primary source context.
Galatians 3:13.dss_contradiction: Tehillim 103:3 — 11QPs: YHWH forgives all transgressions directly. Temple Scroll 11Q19 — Cave 11 addresses the same Devarim passage in its legal context about hanging criminals. The Temple Scroll does not apply this passage to redemption theology. No substitutionary atonement through a curse-bearer appears anywhere in the primary sources.
Galatians 3:13.verdict: A practical legal provision about burial of executed criminals reframed as cosmic redemption theology. The Temple Scroll in the DSS addresses the same passage in its correct legal context. No primary source supports substitutionary atonement.

1 Corinthians 15:3-4.nt_text: Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures; And that he was buried, and that he rose again the third day according to the scriptures.
1 Corinthians 15:3-4.authorship: Among the undisputed Pauline letters. This passage is identified by scholars as a pre-Pauline creedal formula Paul received and passed on — it predates the letter.
1 Corinthians 15:3-4.primary_source_connection: Claimed to be according to the scriptures but no specific DSS text supports the death for sins narrative or the third day resurrection claim
1 Corinthians 15:3-4.original_dss_reading: The texts most commonly cited as supporting these claims: Yeshayahu 53 (collective servant, not individual), Tehillim 22 (lament with vindication, not death prediction), Hoshea 6:2 (national restoration in two days and on the third day, not individual resurrection). None of these in their DSS primary source context support the specific claims made.
1 Corinthians 15:3-4.greco_roman_parallel: Death and resurrection on the third day is documented in the Osiris tradition — killed, three days in the underworld, resurrected by Isis. The dying and rising deity pattern that repeats across Osiris, Dionysus, Tammuz, and Adonis traditions all involve a period of death followed by resurrection. The third day specifically appears in Dionysian tradition.
1 Corinthians 15:3-4.verdict: Claimed to be according to the scriptures but no DSS primary source supports the individual substitutionary death narrative or the third day resurrection claim in its primary source context. The pattern mirrors pre-existing Greco-Roman dying and rising deity traditions.

Ephesians 1:4.nt_text: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.
Ephesians 1:4.authorship: Deutero-Pauline. Ephesians is identified by most NT scholars as written by a disciple of Paul after Paul's death. Vocabulary, sentence structure, and ecclesiology differ significantly from undisputed Pauline letters.
Ephesians 1:4.primary_source_connection: NONE — chosen in a divine human figure before creation has no DSS basis
Ephesians 1:4.dss_contradiction: Wicked and the Holy 4Q181 — Cave 4: The pre-temporal election of the righteous is established by YHWH directly. YHWH chooses His people. No divine human intermediary through whom election occurs appears in any DSS text. The pre-temporal election in 4Q181 is YHWH acting directly not through a chosen human figure.
Ephesians 1:4.verdict: Deutero-Pauline. The concept of election through a divine human intermediary has no DSS basis. Pre-temporal election in the DSS is YHWH's direct action with no intermediary.

2 Timothy 3:16.nt_text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness.
2 Timothy 3:16.authorship: Deutero-Pauline. 2 Timothy is one of the Pastoral Epistles identified by scholars as written after Paul's death by someone using Paul's name. Vocabulary and concerns are inconsistent with undisputed Pauline letters.
2 Timothy 3:16.primary_source_connection: NONE — the claim of divine inspiration for scripture as a category concept
2 Timothy 3:16.dss_contradiction: The irony of this verse is that it is used to claim authority for texts including itself which are demonstrably late anonymous compositions. The DSS Community Rule 1QS describes the authority of the Torah of Moshe and the words of the prophets — specific identified primary sources. The blanket scripture inspiration claim applied to anonymous 2nd century CE Greek documents has no DSS basis. The primary sources distinguish between the Torah, the prophets, and other writings by specific provenance criteria not by a blanket inspiration claim.
2 Timothy 3:16.verdict: Deutero-Pauline. Used to claim authority for the NT canon which was not assembled until 397 CE. The DSS establishes authority through specific manuscript provenance not through blanket inspiration claims applied to anonymous documents.

Absolute Monotheism.text: Before Me no god was formed nor shall there be any after Me. I YHWH am the only one and besides Me there is no saviour.
Absolute Monotheism.contradicts: Any claim of a secondary divine figure, divine son, or co-equal deity

Absolute Monotheism.text: I am the first and I am the last and besides Me there is no god.
Absolute Monotheism.contradicts: Trinity doctrine, divine son theology, divine intermediary figures

Absolute Monotheism.text: I am YHWH and there is no other. Besides Me there is no god. I will strengthen you though you have not known Me, that men may know from the rising to the setting of the sun that there is no one besides Me. I am YHWH and there is no other.
I form the light and create darkness. I make peace and create evil. I YHWH do all these things.
Absolute Monotheism.contradicts: Any independent evil force or devil figure operating outside YHWH's authority

Absolute Monotheism.text: Hear O Yisra'el YHWH is our Creator YHWH is One.
Absolute Monotheism.contradicts: Trinitarian theology, divine son co-equal with YHWH

Absolute Monotheism.text: YHWH He is The Creator. There is no other besides Him.
Absolute Monotheism.contradicts: All polytheistic and semi-polytheistic theological constructs

YHWH as Direct Actor — No Intermediary.text: YHWH will heal the wounded and give life to the dead and bring good news to the poor. He will satisfy the starving ones and lead away the expelled.
YHWH as Direct Actor — No Intermediary.contradicts: The claim that healing and resurrection are performed by a human messiah figure. YHWH is the grammatical subject of every healing act in this text.

YHWH as Direct Actor — No Intermediary.text: Say to those with anxious hearts Be strong do not fear. Behold your Creator will come with vengeance. The recompense of The Creator will come. He will save you. Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
YHWH as Direct Actor — No Intermediary.contradicts: Attribution of healing miracles to a human messiah figure. YHWH acts directly.

YHWH as Direct Actor — No Intermediary.text: He forgives all your transgressions and heals all your diseases.
YHWH as Direct Actor — No Intermediary.contradicts: Salvation through blood sacrifice of a divine human intermediary. YHWH forgives directly.

Human Messiah Only.text: Until the coming of the Prophet and the anointed ones of Aharon and Yisra'el.
Human Messiah Only.contradicts: A single divine messiah. The DSS expects multiple human anointed figures — a priestly anointed one and a royal anointed one — both human, both mortal.

Human Messiah Only.text: The anointed one of Aharon and Yisra'el shall arise and atone for their iniquity.
Human Messiah Only.contradicts: A divine suffering saviour. The anointed figure in the Damascus Document is a future human priestly-royal figure within the covenant community structure.

Human Messiah Only.text: The Prince of the Congregation shall advance and YHWH shall fight for Yisra'el.
Human Messiah Only.contradicts: The messiah as divine saviour who defeats evil through supernatural power. The human Prince advances. YHWH fights. The distinction is explicit.

Solar Calendar — YHWH's Appointed Times.text: Command the children of Yisra'el that they observe the years according to this reckoning — three hundred and sixty-four days. These will constitute a complete year. They will not disturb its seasons from its days and from its festivals for everything will fall out in them according to their testimony. They will not leave out any day nor disturb any festivals.
Solar Calendar — YHWH's Appointed Times.contradicts: All lunisolar calendar systems including the Rabbinic calendar which shifts festival dates from year to year.

Solar Calendar — YHWH's Appointed Times.text: Blessed are all the righteous and blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun travels in the heaven coming in and going out each month with a full three hundred and sixty-four days.
Solar Calendar — YHWH's Appointed Times.contradicts: Lunar calendar systems used by Rabbinic tradition and Christian liturgical calendars.

False Prophet Test.text: But the prophet who speaks a word presumptuously in My name which I have not commanded him to speak or which he speaks in the name of other gods that prophet shall die. You may say in your heart How will we know the word which YHWH has not spoken? When a prophet speaks in the name of YHWH if the thing does not come about or come true that is the thing which YHWH has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously.
False Prophet Test.contradicts: Predictions the NT attributes to its invented figure that did not come to pass within the stated timeframe: the end of the age within the generation of his disciples (Matthew 24:34), the coming of the Son of Man before the disciples finished their circuit of the towns of Yisra'el (Matthew 10:23), the destruction of the temple within a generation (Matthew 24:34).

Virgin Birth Contradicted.text: Behold the almah shall conceive and bear a son and shall call his name Immanuel.
Virgin Birth Contradicted.contradicts: The virgin birth claim. Almah means young woman of marriageable age. The Hebrew word for virgin is betulah. Betulah does not appear in this verse in any ancient manuscript. The DSS primary witness is unambiguous.

Virgin Birth Contradicted.text: I will put enmity between you and the woman and between your seed and her seed. He shall strike you on the head and you shall strike him on the heel.
Virgin Birth Contradicted.contradicts: The interpretation of seed as a reference to a virgin-born messiah. The primary source uses the ordinary word for seed meaning offspring or descendants. No supernatural birth is indicated.

Resurrection — YHWH Acts Directly.text: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake some to everlasting life and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Resurrection — YHWH Acts Directly.contradicts: Resurrection through a divine human intermediary. YHWH raises. No intermediary figure performs the resurrection in any DSS text.

Resurrection — YHWH Acts Directly.text: Behold I will open your graves and raise you from your graves O My people and I will bring you into the land of Yisra'el. Then you will know that I am YHWH when I have opened your graves and raised you from your graves O My people. I will put My spirit within you and you will come to life.
Resurrection — YHWH Acts Directly.contradicts: Resurrection as an act of a divine human saviour. YHWH opens the graves. YHWH raises. YHWH puts His spirit within. No intermediary.

Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.text: I am YHWH who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by Myself.
Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.contradicts: Any claim that a pre-existent divine figure participated in creation. YHWH created alone. By Himself. No pre-existent son, Logos, or divine agent. 1QIsa-a is the primary witness.

Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.text: It is I who made the earth and created mankind upon it. My own hands stretched out the heavens and I marshaled their starry hosts.
Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.contradicts: John 1:3 which claims all things were created through a pre-existent divine Word figure. YHWH's own hands created. No intermediary.

Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.ms: DSS Yirmeyahu — shorter than Masoretic, DSS is primary
Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.text: YHWH made the earth by His power; He founded the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
Pre-Existence Claims Contradicted.contradicts: Pre-existent creative intermediary. YHWH's own power, wisdom, and understanding created. No divine son agent.

Divine Sonship Contradicted.text: Then say to Pharaoh: This is what YHWH says: Yisra’el is My firstborn son.
Divine Sonship Contradicted.contradicts: The claim that a single individual is uniquely the Son of YHWH. In the primary sources Yisra’el collectively is YHWH's firstborn son. This is a covenant relationship applied to the nation, not a biological or metaphysical claim about an individual.

Divine Sonship Contradicted.text: I will declare the decree: YHWH has said to me, You are My son; today I have begotten you.
Divine Sonship Contradicted.contradicts: The NT application of this to a divine individual. In the DSS context Tehillim 2 is a royal enthronement psalm. The you are My son declaration is the covenant language of royal adoption spoken to the Davidic king at his coronation. Every Davidic king was declared YHWH's son at enthronement. This is covenant language not biological divinity.

Divine Sonship Contradicted.text: When Yisra’el was a child I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.
Divine Sonship Contradicted.contradicts: The NT application in Matthew 2:15 which applies this verse to an individual child. The DSS context is unambiguous: YHWH is speaking about the collective nation of Yisra’el being called out of Egypt in the Exodus. It is not a prediction about an individual. It is a historical statement about the nation.

Eternal Hellfire Contradicted.text: The dead do not praise YHWH, nor do any who go down into silence.
Eternal Hellfire Contradicted.contradicts: Eternal conscious torment in hellfire. The dead are in silence. Not in anguish. Not conscious. Sheol in the DSS is the realm of the dead characterized by silence and inactivity, not by eternal torment.

Eternal Hellfire Contradicted.text: For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing, and they have no more reward, for the memory of them is forgotten.
Eternal Hellfire Contradicted.contradicts: Eternal conscious existence in hell or heaven immediately after death. The dead know nothing. This is the primary source framework: death is a state of unknowing, not continued conscious existence in a place of reward or punishment.

Eternal Hellfire Contradicted.text: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
Eternal Hellfire Contradicted.contradicts: The Greek Hades / Roman Tartarus eternal torment framework. The DSS Daniyyel presents resurrection as a future event from sleep in the dust, not as immediate post-death conscious torment. The judgment is at the resurrection, not at the moment of death.

Original Sin Contradicted.text: The soul who sins is the one who will die. The son will not share the guilt of the father, nor will the father share the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous man will be credited to him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be charged against him.
Original Sin Contradicted.contradicts: The doctrine of inherited original sin from Adam. YHWH states explicitly through Yehezkel that guilt is individual and not inherited. The son does not share the father's guilt. This directly and explicitly contradicts the Augustinian doctrine of inherited Adamic guilt.

Original Sin Contradicted.text: Parents are not to be put to death for their children, nor children put to death for their parents; each will die for their own sin.
Original Sin Contradicted.contradicts: Inherited original sin. The Torah law is explicit: each person dies for their own sin. Not for an ancestor's sin. Not for Adam's sin. This is the primary source legal standard directly contradicting the original sin doctrine.

Original Sin Contradicted.text: YHWH created humanity and appointed two spirits in which to walk until the time of His visitation: the Spirit of Truth and the Spirit of Iniquity. The nature of all the children of humanity is ruled by these two spirits.
Original Sin Contradicted.contradicts: Original sin as inherited guilt corrupting human nature at birth. The DSS Two Spirits framework presents human moral struggle as the result of two appointed spirits governing human choices, not as inherited corruption from a single ancestral sin.

timeline.label: DSS Primary Texts Written
timeline.desc: Dead Sea Scrolls composed at Qumran. Physical manuscripts sealed in caves. Primary source in ancient Hebrew and Aramaic.

timeline.label: Septuagint Greek Translation
timeline.desc: Hebrew texts translated into Greek for diaspora Jewish communities. Translation diverges from Hebrew at multiple points. Almah becomes parthenos. Sons of El becomes Sons of Yisra'el. These divergences become the textual foundation of later NT claims.

timeline.label: NT Texts Written in Greek
timeline.desc: NT documents composed in Greek by Greek-speaking communities. Authors use Septuagint not Hebrew originals. Theological claims built on Greek translation errors and Greco-Roman religious frameworks.

timeline.label: DSS Sealed in Caves
timeline.desc: Qumran community dispersed. Scrolls hidden in 11 caves. Inaccessible to all subsequent communities including NT authors. NT writers had no access to the DSS.

timeline.label: Gospel Names Assigned
timeline.desc: Irenaeus of Lyon assigns names Matthew, Mark, Luke, John to four anonymous gospels for theological reasons he states explicitly — four gospels to match four winds and four corners of the earth. No historical evidence for these attributions.

timeline.label: Council of Nicaea
timeline.desc: Convened by Roman Emperor Constantine. Divinity of Yeshua affirmed by vote. Arian position declared heresy. Nicene Creed formulated as political settlement. Trinity doctrine institutionalized. Canon not yet finalized.

timeline.label: Council of Carthage — NT Canon Finalized
timeline.desc: 27-book NT canon formally established. Multiple texts previously in circulation removed. Books excluded include Shepherd of Hermas, Epistle of Barnabas, Didache, Gospel of Peter, Gospel of Thomas. Selection criteria: apostolic authorship (already shown to be false for all books) and theological conformity with established doctrine.

timeline.label: Latin Vulgate — Jerome's Translation
timeline.desc: Jerome translates the NT into Latin. Introduces the translation error in Romans 5:12 that becomes the basis of Augustine's original sin doctrine — in whom all sinned instead of because all sinned. Changes the meaning of the entire passage.

timeline.label: Johannine Comma First Appears
timeline.desc: The Trinitarian verse 1 John 5:7 — Father, Word, and Holy Ghost — appears for the first time in a Latin manuscript. Absent from all Greek manuscripts. Absent from all early church fathers. A scribe insertion that becomes the clearest Trinitarian statement in the entire NT.

timeline.label: Masoretic Text Compiled
timeline.desc: Rabbinic scholars compile the standardized Hebrew Bible text with vowel pointing system. Text diverges from DSS at hundreds of points. Devarim 32:8 changes Sons of El to Sons of Yisra'el. Multiple other alterations documented.

timeline.label: Dead Sea Scrolls Discovered
timeline.desc: Scrolls found in 11 caves at Qumran. 981 texts recovered. Publication controlled by small Western Christian academic team for 40 years. Full public access delayed until 1990s. The primary source evidence that predates and contradicts the NT theological architecture becomes available to scholars.

timeline.label: DSS Publication Suppressed
timeline.desc: Only a small team of scholars had access to the full scroll corpus for nearly 40 years after discovery. Fragments were parceled out to individual scholars who held exclusive rights. The full corpus was not made publicly available until the Huntington Library released photographs in 1991 against the official team's objections.

apocrypha_audit.convened_by: Roman Emperor Constantine — a political ruler who wanted religious unity in the empire
apocrypha_audit.political_context: Constantine had recently converted to Christianity but maintained pagan practices simultaneously. He needed religious unity to stabilize his empire. The theological dispute between Arius (who denied divine equality of the Son) and Alexander of Alexandria (who affirmed it) was causing civil unrest. Constantine called the council to resolve the dispute politically.
apocrypha_audit.books_excluded: The council did not formally canonize the NT — that came later — but established the theological framework that determined what would be excluded. Arian texts, texts questioning the divinity of Yeshua, and texts affirming strict monotheism were declared heretical.
apocrypha_audit.what_was_suppressed: Any theological position affirming that YHWH is One and no secondary divine figure exists co-equal with Him. The Arian position which affirmed that the Son was a created being subordinate to the Father — closer to the DSS framework — was declared heresy by vote.

apocrypha_audit.convened_by: North African bishops under Roman church authority
apocrypha_audit.political_context: Multiple competing canons existed across the ancient Christian world. Unification of the canon was necessary for institutional authority. Books were included or excluded based on theological conformity with established doctrine, not historical authenticity.
books_excluded: Shepherd of Hermas — widely read in early communities, promoted rigorous monotheism, questioned eternal punishment
Epistle of Barnabas — claimed the Jews had forfeited their covenant — too anti-Jewish even for the institutional church at that stage
Didache — practical early community document, no divine saviour theology
Gospel of Peter — presented by some scholars as potentially older than the canonical gospels
Gospel of Thomas — 114 sayings attributed to the NT figure, no birth narrative, no resurrection narrative, no theology of salvation through blood
Gospel of Philip — Gnostic, too philosophical
Acts of Paul and Thecla — featured a woman as central authority figure, incompatible with institutionalizing male church hierarchy
apocrypha_audit.what_was_suppressed: Any text that: questioned the necessity of institutional church for salvation, affirmed female religious authority, lacked a divine saviour theology, or presented the NT figure as a wisdom teacher rather than a divine being constructed by Rome.

apocrypha_audit.convened_by: Catholic Church in response to Protestant Reformation
apocrypha_audit.political_context: Protestant reformers were rejecting Catholic authority and using the Hebrew Bible directly. The Council of Trent reaffirmed the Deuterocanonical books (called Apocrypha by Protestants) to maintain Catholic theological positions that depended on them — particularly 2 Maccabees 12:46 which supports prayers for the dead and therefore Purgatory doctrine.
apocrypha_audit.books_excluded: Protestant reformers following Luther excluded the Deuterocanonical books from the Hebrew Bible canon because they were not in the Hebrew DSS corpus. Luther correctly identified that 1 and 2 Maccabees, Tobit, Judith, Wisdom of Solomon, Sirach, and Baruch were not in the ancient Hebrew primary source tradition. However the Protestant reformers retained the NT canon established at Carthage 397 CE without questioning its authenticity.
apocrypha_audit.what_was_suppressed: The DSS primary source tradition itself. Both Catholic and Protestant traditions in 1546 were working from Latin translations of Greek texts removed by two to three translation stages from the ancient Hebrew originals. The actual primary sources — the DSS — were still sealed in caves and would not be discovered for another 400 years.

meta.sources: DSS primary — Orit Ge'ez primary — historical manuscript evidence only
meta.rules: YHWH and The Creator only. No Lord. No God. No Rabbinic framing. No Christian overlay. Facts and manuscript evidence only.

restoration_path.description: For every manipulated passage, shows the user how to read it correctly in its original primary source context.
restoration_path.method: Returning the passage to its literary context, its historical situation, its manuscript evidence, and its covenant framework.

entries.corrupted_reading: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son as a prediction of a future individual birth.
entries.restoration: The almah in 1QIsa-a Cave 1 is a young woman contemporary to King Ahaz. The sign is given to Ahaz about events in his lifetime during the Syro-Ephraimite crisis 735 BCE. The child Immanuel is a covenant sign of YHWH's protection of Yehudah in that specific historical crisis. Read the surrounding verses: 7:1-16 address Ahaz and his current political situation. The passage is complete within that historical context.

entries.corrupted_reading: A prediction of an individual's death experience extracted from the opening cry of abandonment.
entries.restoration: Tehillim 22 is a communal lament psalm used in worship. It opens with crisis and moves to resolution. The full psalm must be read: verses 1-21 are the cry of distress, verses 22-31 are the vindication and praise. The psalm ends with YHWH answering and the community praising. Reading only verse 1 severs the psalm from its resolution. The full text in 11QPs Cave 11 shows a psalm of trust, not abandonment.

entries.corrupted_reading: An individual suffering saviour extracted from its literary unit.
entries.restoration: Yeshayahu 53 is one chapter within the Servant Songs of Yeshayahu 40-55. The servant is identified as Yisra’el explicitly in Yeshayahu 41:8, 44:1, 44:21, 45:4, 48:20, 49:3. Chapter 53 is part of this continuous literary unit. Reading it within the full 16-chapter Servant Song context reveals the suffering and vindication of the covenant nation of Yisra’el, not an individual.

entries.corrupted_reading: A prediction of a specific individual messianic prophet.
entries.restoration: YHWH tells Moshe He will raise up prophets like Moshe from among the brothers. The Hebrew is plural in structure and context: a succession of prophets in the tradition of Moshe, not one specific individual. The immediate context in Devarim 18:20-22 then gives the test for a true prophet: if what he says does not come to pass he has spoken presumptuously. This test applies to every prophet in the succession including any claimed to fulfil verse 15.

audio_pronunciation_guide.description: Every ancient Hebrew, Aramaic, and Ge'ez term has phonetic pronunciation in original language phonetics, not modern Israeli Hebrew.
audio_pronunciation_guide.note: Modern Israeli Hebrew pronunciation postdates the DSS by two thousand years and reflects Ashkenazi and Sephardic European pronunciation patterns. The original phonetics of the DSS era are reconstructed from: comparative Semitic linguistics, Akkadian cuneiform transliterations of Hebrew names, ancient Greek transliterations, and the vocalization patterns preserved in the Yemenite Jewish tradition which is closest to ancient pronunciation.

terms.phonetic: Yah-weh or Yah-hoo-eh (reconstructed from ancient Greek Iaue and Iabe)
terms.note: The exact pronunciation was not vocalized in ancient scrolls. The name appears as four consonants only.
Raz: R as in run, A as in father, Z as in zone. Nihyeh: Nih as in knee, YEH rhymes with yeah.
Ayin is a pharyngeal consonant. In ancient pronunciation it was a distinct consonant, not a glottal stop as in modern Israeli Hebrew.
The Bet has a V sound between vowels in ancient pronunciation.
Shin as in shoe. Ayin at the end was an audible pharyngeal consonant in ancient pronunciation.
Long I sound. The Tav at the end was pronounced as T not S in ancient Hebrew.
The Tzadi is a emphatic S-Z sound. Qof is an emphatic K pronounced further back in the throat than standard K.
